description: ClearExams source-linked notes for 25 November 2026 cover Cabinet infrastructure and postal decisions, Tamil Nadu's Kamarajar Port terminal, aviation cooperation, statistics, science, rural governance, water-sector skills and India-Nepal defence cooperation.

stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹11,000-crore construction-equipment manufacturing scheme
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved an eight-year Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment Manufacturing Ecosystem, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries. The approval provides incentives for eligible equipment and component makers and support for a dedicated testing facility; it is an approved scheme, not a report of factories already established.
key_facts: The scheme has a financial outlay of ₹11,000 crore and runs from FY 2026-27 to FY 2033-34.
Its sales-linked incentives are graded from 13% to 8% of incremental sales over five years for approved OEMs and component manufacturers.
A grant of up to ₹375 crore is provided as viability-gap funding for a dedicated construction-equipment testing facility.
The official release placed India third globally in the sector, after China and the United States, with a FY 2024-25 market size of about ₹97,500 crore.
stories.exam_link: Revise production-linked incentives, viability-gap funding, capital-goods manufacturing and the role of the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
stories.source_title: PIB: Cabinet approves ₹11,000 crore CIE manufacturing ecosystem scheme, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Second container terminal approved for Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the proposed second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under public-private partnership on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer basis. The decision authorises development of the project; it does not mean that the terminal has already been built or commissioned.
key_facts: The estimated project cost is ₹4,288.26 crore, including GST.
The planned terminal is 900 metres long, has an 18-metre design draft and is to be implemented in two phases.
Its planned annual handling capacity is 2.0 million twenty-foot equivalent units.
Kamarajar Port, formerly Ennore Port, is one of India's 12 major ports and is wholly owned by the Chennai Port Authority.
stories.exam_link: Revise India's major ports, Chennai-Ennore port geography, PPP models, DBFOT concessions and the meaning of TEU in container trade.
stories.source_title: PIB: CCEA approves second container terminal at Kamarajar Port, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Greenfield airport approved at Doloo near Silchar in Assam
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved development of a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Cachar district, Assam, by the Airports Authority of India. The project is intended to address the constraints of the existing defence-landlocked civil enclave at Silchar and improve connectivity for the Barak Valley.
key_facts: The estimated project cost is ₹2,014 crore.
The proposed terminal building covers 12,351 square metres and is designed for 800 passengers during the peak hour.
The planned runway is 2,705 metres by 45 metres, Code 4C compliant and suitable for A320 aircraft.
Doloo is in Cachar district, within Assam's Barak Valley.
stories.exam_link: Revise greenfield versus brownfield airports, the Airports Authority of India, Assam's Barak Valley and ICAO aerodrome reference codes.
stories.source_title: PIB: Greenfield airport at Doloo, Silchar approved, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Postal Operations Scheme continued for the Sixteenth Finance Commission cycle
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the Central Sector Postal Operations Scheme from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme is designed to modernise mail and parcel operations, support e-commerce logistics, strengthen rural connectivity and expand digital and citizen-facing services delivered through India Post.
key_facts: The approved outlay is ₹1,141 crore for the five-year period.
Mail Network Optimization receives ₹575 crore for centralised delivery, mechanisation, GIS-based services and Advanced Postal Technology 2.0.
India Post also delivers savings-bank, payments-bank, insurance, Aadhaar, passport and export-support services.
This is a Central Sector Scheme, meaning it is funded by the Union government.
stories.exam_link: Revise the difference between Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes, India Post's public-service role and the Sixteenth Finance Commission cycle.
stories.source_title: PIB: Postal Operations Scheme continued with ₹1,141 crore outlay, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Cabinet clears India-Singapore aviation MRO cooperation memorandum
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved signing an India-Singapore memorandum on skills and industry development in aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul. The proposed cooperation establishes a framework for training and industrial partnerships; the Cabinet approval is not itself evidence that the facilities or training programmes have already been completed.
key_facts: The framework covers joint development of an industry-oriented Aircraft Maintenance Engineer curriculum.
It provides for capacity building of Indian institutes and internships or exchanges with Singapore MRO entities.
It also facilitates partnerships between Indian and Singaporean stakeholders to support expansion of MRO facilities.
MRO stands for maintenance, repair and overhaul.
stories.exam_link: Revise India-Singapore relations, civil-aviation regulation, Aircraft Maintenance Engineers and how domestic MRO capacity affects airline costs and aircraft downtime.
stories.source_title: PIB: Cabinet approves India-Singapore aviation MRO MoU, 25 November 2026

stories.title: North-East-specific antivenom developed for two pit-viper species
stories.summary: Scientists developed an antivenom specifically effective against venom from Pope's pit viper and the red-tailed bamboo pit viper, two medically significant species found in North-Eastern India. The development addresses a treatment gap because conventional Indian polyvalent antivenom mainly targets the country's traditional 'Big Four' snake species.
key_facts: The targeted species are Trimeresurus popeiorum and Trimeresurus erythrurus.
Commercial polyvalent antivenom in India primarily targets the spectacled cobra, common krait, Russell's viper and saw-scaled viper.
Pit-viper bites are an important medical emergency in parts of North-Eastern India.
Species-specific venom variation is a major reason that antivenom effectiveness can differ across regions.
stories.exam_link: Revise antibodies and antivenom, venomous-snake diversity, the 'Big Four' of India and the biodiversity significance of the North-Eastern region.
stories.source_title: PIB: First North-East India-specific antivenom for neglected pit vipers, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Nayi Chetna 5.0 launched as nationwide gender-equality campaign
stories.summary: The fifth edition of Nayi Chetna: Pahal Badlaav Ki was launched as a nationwide, community-led campaign on gender equality and women's empowerment. Led through DAY-NRLM institutions, the campaign is scheduled across all States and Union Territories from 25 November to 23 December 2026 and is supported by an inter-ministerial approach.
key_facts: Fifteen Union ministries and departments are participating in the campaign.
Its four stated themes are Identity, Assetization, Mobility and Redistribution of Unpaid Care Work.
Self-help groups and community institutions will use meetings, rallies, street plays and dialogues with men and youth.
The launch release reported 5.3 crore participants and nearly 7,000 Gender Resource Centres across earlier editions.
stories.exam_link: Revise DAY-NRLM, self-help groups, gender budgeting, unpaid care work and institutional support such as Women Helpline 181 and One Stop Centres.

stories.title: India-Nepal joint military exercise Suryakiran XX begins in Nepal
stories.summary: The twentieth edition of Exercise Suryakiran commenced at the Nepal Army Battle School in Saljhandi. The annual bilateral exercise is being conducted from 25 November to 8 December 2026 to strengthen interoperability in counter-insurgency, counter-terrorism, disaster response and medical training.
key_facts: India fielded 334 personnel from the Kumaon Regiment, while Nepal fielded an equal-strength contingent from Shri Jawla Dal Battalion.
Training includes tactical and heliborne operations, disaster response and medical drills.
Exercise Suryakiran is held alternately in India and Nepal.
Saljhandi is the location of the Nepal Army Battle School hosting this edition.
stories.exam_link: Revise India-Nepal defence cooperation, bilateral military exercises, the Kumaon Regiment and the concept of interoperability between armed forces.
stories.source_title: PIB: India-Nepal Exercise Suryakiran XX commences, 25 November 2026

stories.title: MoSPI and DSCI sign memorandum on trusted data sharing for statistics
stories.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and the Data Security Council of India signed a memorandum to develop trusted data-sharing practices for official statistics. The partnership will prepare policy and technical work on privacy, confidentiality, data quality and the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.
key_facts: DSCI is a not-for-profit industry body and think tank set up by Nasscom.
The first planned output is a policy paper on trusted data flows and data management, drawing on international good practices.
The cooperation covers privacy-enhancing technologies, responsible AI and pilot projects with research, academic and industry partners.
The memorandum supports the wider National Statistical System.
stories.exam_link: Revise the National Statistical System, MoSPI, data governance, statistical confidentiality and privacy-enhancing technologies.
stories.source_title: PIB: MoSPI and DSCI sign trusted-data-sharing MoU, 25 November 2026

stories.title: MoSPI tracks 1,862 major Central Sector infrastructure projects
stories.summary: MoSPI's October 2026 Monthly Flash Report covered Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore or more. It reported 1,862 monitored projects with a latest total project cost of ₹38.11 lakh crore and expenditure of ₹17.87 lakh crore, offering a snapshot of implementation rather than announcing a new spending scheme.
key_facts: Recorded expenditure was about 46.88% of the latest combined project cost.
Transport and logistics plus energy accounted for 1,553 projects, or 83.41% of the total number monitored.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways had 972 projects, the largest count among ministries.
The report's monitoring threshold is ₹150 crore and above.
stories.exam_link: Revise infrastructure project monitoring, time and cost overruns, Central Sector investment and MoSPI's role in official project statistics.
stories.source_title: PIB: October 2026 flash report on Central Sector infrastructure projects, 25 November 2026

stories.title: Regional Accounts report issued for the 2022-23 national-accounts series
stories.summary: MoSPI released the report of the Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts connected with the 2022-23 series of National Accounts. The committee reviewed concepts, classifications, data sources and estimation methods for State Domestic Product and District Domestic Product under the revised statistical framework.
key_facts: The national-accounts base year is being revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23.
The Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics is chaired by Professor B. N. Goldar.
Five sub-committees were constituted for areas including new data sources, methodology, constant prices, regional accounts and the SNA 2025 update.
State Domestic Product and District Domestic Product are regional counterparts used to measure economic activity below the national level.
stories.exam_link: Revise GDP, GSDP, DDP, base-year revision, constant-price estimates and the role of the National Statistical Office within MoSPI.
stories.source_title: PIB: Report of Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts released, 25 November 2026

stories.title: MoU targets skilling one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
stories.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation signed a memorandum with the Directorate General of Training to train and certify at least one lakh candidates during the extended Jal Jeevan Mission period. The collaboration is a capacity-building plan for operation and maintenance of rural water-supply systems, not a claim that all candidates have already been trained.
key_facts: The minimum training and certification target is 1,00,000 candidates.
The estimated outlay is about ₹111.93 crore, to be borne by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
The Directorate General of Training functions under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
Jal Jeevan Mission focuses on rural household tap-water supply and the sustainability of village water systems.
stories.exam_link: Revise Jal Jeevan Mission, rural drinking-water governance, village-level operation and maintenance and India's vocational-training institutional structure.
stories.source_title: PIB: DDWS-DGT MoU to skill one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, 25 November 2026

mcqs.question: Which ministry will implement the approved ₹11,000-crore construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing scheme?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
mcqs.explanation: The Ministry of Heavy Industries is the implementing ministry for the CIE manufacturing ecosystem scheme.

mcqs.question: The approved second container terminal at Kamarajar Port is planned under which concession model?
options: Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer
mcqs.explanation: The project was approved under PPP on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer basis.

mcqs.question: Kamarajar Port, formerly known as Ennore Port, is wholly owned by which port authority?
mcqs.explanation: Kamarajar Port Limited is wholly owned by the Chennai Port Authority.

mcqs.question: The new greenfield airport approved at Doloo is intended to serve which Assam region?
mcqs.explanation: Doloo lies in Cachar district and the airport is designed to improve connectivity for the Barak Valley.

mcqs.question: What is the approved outlay for continuation of the Postal Operations Scheme during FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31?
mcqs.explanation: The Cabinet approved ₹1,141 crore for the Central Sector Postal Operations Scheme over the stated cycle.

mcqs.question: In civil aviation, the abbreviation MRO expands to which phrase?
mcqs.explanation: MRO means maintenance, repair and overhaul of aircraft and components.

mcqs.question: The newly reported North-East-specific antivenom targets Pope's pit viper and which other species?
mcqs.explanation: It targets Pope's pit viper and the red-tailed bamboo pit viper.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not one of India's conventional 'Big Four' snakes targeted by common polyvalent antivenom?
mcqs.explanation: The red-tailed bamboo pit viper is outside the conventional Big Four.

mcqs.question: Nayi Chetna 5.0 is led through institutions associated with which programme?
mcqs.explanation: The gender-equality campaign is led through DAY-NRLM self-help-group and community institutions.

mcqs.question: Exercise Suryakiran is an annual bilateral military exercise between India and which country?
mcqs.explanation: Suryakiran is conducted alternately in India and Nepal by their armies.

mcqs.question: Which Indian Army regiment represented India at Exercise Suryakiran XX?
mcqs.explanation: The Indian contingent of 334 personnel was drawn from the Kumaon Regiment.

mcqs.question: The Data Security Council of India, which signed a data-sharing MoU with MoSPI, was set up by which organisation?
mcqs.explanation: DSCI is a not-for-profit industry body and think tank set up by Nasscom.

mcqs.question: MoSPI's October 2026 infrastructure flash report monitored projects with a cost of at least what amount?
mcqs.explanation: The report covers Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore and above.

mcqs.question: India's National Accounts base year is being revised from 2011-12 to which year?
mcqs.explanation: The revised National Accounts series uses FY 2022-23 as its base year.

mcqs.question: The Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 skills memorandum aims to train and certify at least how many candidates?
mcqs.explanation: The DDWS-DGT memorandum sets a minimum target of one lakh candidates.
